stories.headline: Udhayanidhi Stalin held for 'sexual remark' linking CM Vijay; freed on bail hours later
stories.bodyText:
CHENNAI/THANJAVUR: Former Tamil Nadu deputy chief minister Udhayanidhi Stalin was on Tuesday arrested for his alleged double entendre alluding to a popular female actor. He was released later in the evening on station bail.
Udhayanidhi, TVK supporters said, had made a sexually loaded remark linking CM Joseph Vijay with an actress whose name the crowd was chanting at a Cauvery protest in Thanjavur Monday. Udhayanidhi denied the charge.
On Tuesday morning, police knocked on the DMK politician's door at Neelankarai, Chennai. Before his lawyers could move Madras high court for anticipatory bail, Udhayanidhi was taken away in a police van for a seven-hour ride to Thanjavur where the complaint was filed by a TVK backer.
He was charged under Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sec 67 of the Information Technology Act for "promoting social enmity, harassment and electronic obscenity". He was also charged on seven counts under the BNS, including Sec 79 (insult to a woman's modesty).
"This is a joke," Udhayanidhi said before being taken away. "We will fight this case legally." The police van came to a crawl at many places as DMK cadres blocked the highway raising slogans against the TVK govt. 
Cadres also staged protests across the state.
AIADMK joins DMK in slamming Udhaya arrest
Late in the evening, Udhayanidhi was released after being questioned by Thanjavur police. DMK supporters showered petals and raised slogans.
DMK president M K Stalin called the arrest an act of arrogance. “They have arrested him to prevent the leader of the opposition from attending the assembly when the budget is tabled,” he said. Stalin said Udhayanidhi neither referred to anyone in his speech nor made obscene remarks. “Some politicians condemning him for a remark which he never made is to divert attention from real issues,’’ he said.
AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami criticised Udhayanidhi for the offensive remark but condemned the arrest as it was done the day before the state budget was to be tabled. “This attempt to hold the assembly session without the leader of opposition is highly condemnable,” EPS said.
Around 7.20am, Thanjavur police arrived at Udhayanidhi’s Neelankarai residence. Soon, Stalin’s son-in-law, V Sabareesan, senior DMK politicians and a legal team arrived at the house objecting to the police action. They approached the Madras high court seeking urgent hearing of an anticipatory bail plea around 10.25am. Justice G K Ilanthiraiyan agreed to take up the plea at noon and orally instructed police not to precipitate the issue until then.
However, police arrested Udhayanidhi and were en route Thanjavur by the time the court took up the case for hearing at 2.15pm. Advocate-general Vijay Narayan told the court that the state govt has no intention to remand Udhayanidhi, and that he would be released on station bail after questioning.
The police entourage reached Thanjavur around 6.30pm. Since DMK cadres had thronged Thanjavur East police station, where the case was registered, police took Udhayanidhi to Sengipatti station. He was questioned there for more than an hour by a police team led by Thanjavur SP E Sundaravadanam and released around 8.10pm. Udhayanidhi got a loud reception by DMK cadres outside the police station before heading for Trichy airport. He took the day’s last flight to Chennai.

stories.headline: From Launch To Data, Tech To Isro Facility Use, Pvt Cos To Get 30-100% Subsidy
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Indian private space companies and non-govt entities will receive govt support ranging from 30% to 100% on everything from launch services and technology transfer to satellite data and access to 
Isro
 facilities under two new schemes of the Department of Space (DoS).
The incentives — Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and the Price Support Scheme — being implemented by Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) are aimed at lowering entry barriers, making Indian space businesses globally competitive and accelerating private participation across the sector.
The larger of the two initiatives is the Launch Services Price-support Scheme, with a budget of Rs 800 crore over five years until June 2031. The scheme seeks to boost domestic commercial launch operations and strengthen India’s position as a global launch hub.
IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka told 
TOI
: “The idea is to make the launches competitive. Therefore, we are trying to defray the cost of launch, thereby making the launch cost globally competitive. The ultimate beneficiary will be the satellite launch.”
Under Category A, eligible entities can receive up to 50% support for using Isro and DoS launch facilities. 
The benefit extends to NGEs, government entities and launch vehicle providers.
Category B offers a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower, for Indian small launch vehicles carrying satellites, experiments or payloads weighing up to 500 kg. The support is available to satellite owners and operators.
The subsidy would apply to launches by Indian private entities from Indian soil too. “It will be applicable to [Skyroot’s] Vikram also. Any satellite launch by an Indian company... from Indian soil... we will directly pay the satellite guys $3,000 per kg,” Goenka said. He added that the policy is focused on promoting small launch vehicles where private sector participation is growing.
Category C provides the highest level of support, offering 100% funding for repurposed upper-stage platforms carrying payloads of up to 120 kg. The funding is capped at $13,000 per kg and limited to four missions. The category is aimed at NGEs, govt entities and launch vehicle providers.
Category D extends launch incentives to satellites weighing up to 100 kg launched aboard PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 missions. Beneficiaries will receive a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower.
Complementing the launch incentives is a separate Price Support Scheme for Indian entities, which will run for three years until Feb 2029. The programme is intended to reduce the cost of accessing India’s space infrastructure, technologies and data.
The scheme has three components. The first provides up to 50% support for the utilisation of DoS and In-SPACe facilities, along with technical expertise.
The second offers a 30% subsidy on Technology Transfer Fees (TTF) for technologies licensed from Isro, lowering the cost for companies seeking to commercialise govt-developed technologies.
The third provides a 50% subsidy on standard Earth Observation data and data products, making satellite imagery and geospatial datasets more affordable for Indian companies developing applications in agriculture, urban planning, disaster management, climate services and other downstream sectors.

stories.headline: Scrolls, satire and superheroes: Inside 1500 years of Indian storytelling
stories.deck: From Amar Chitra Katha to graphic novels, a new exhibition maps the evolution of how India has told its stories
stories.bodyText:
"India has always been a nation of storytellers," says Amruta Patil, one of India's acclaimed graphic novelists and the curator of A Moving Line, an exhibition that gathers more than 250 works to trace 1500 years of Indian storytelling at the Museum of Art and Photography (MAP), Bengaluru. "Long before comic books, graphic novels and social media, stories travelled through painted scrolls, temple walls and travelling performers. A Moving Line aims to bring together the unbroken thread of Indian storytelling that spans ancient tales, comics and digital narratives," she adds.
Where it all began
The exhibition opens with ancient traditions such as 
Kaavad
 and 
Pattachitra
. Unlike Western comics, these storytelling forms reveal themselves in layers, inviting viewers to travel through the narrative at their own pace. Mythology, trade, religious patronage and history have all shaped Indian visual culture, and these stories transcended language and regional boundaries, creating a visual vocabulary long before print arrived.
How comics became a part of Indian culture
One of the exhibition’s most engaging sections revisits the birth of Indian comics. "And at the heart of this section is Amar Chitra Katha (ACK) whose creator, Anant Pai, silently birthed a cultural revival in Udupi. 
Fondly known as Uncle Pai, he used Amar Chitra Katha to break free from the postcolonial mindset of the era and reconnect India to its forgotten myths, folklore and stories. Comics became more than just children's entertainment. They became cultural ambassadors," she says, adding that as society evolves, so do its stories. "Contemporary creators are revisiting mythology through a fresh lens — feminist, queer and socially conscious — without dismissing the originals."
When cartoons became political
Another interesting section explores India's long history of political cartoons. Beginning with early Bengali cartoons inspired by Punch magazine, the exhibition traces how satire became one of the country’s most effective forms of public commentary. Political cartoons, editorial illustrations and graphic satire emerge here not merely as humour, but as powerful tools of dissent and social criticism. "It was primarily to challenge the bourgeois mindset," points out Amruta.
The works of India's foremost female cartoonist, Sukhalata Rao — aunt of Satyajit Ray — also find a place here. What's also noteworthy is the influence of Bollywood in shaping popular culture through comics like 
Bahadur
 and 
Supremo
. Bahadur is an orphan who grows up to become a courageous man as the series champions education, women empowerment and rural development. Amitabh Bachchan features as a superhero in 
Supremo
. The character was conceived by Pammi Bakshi with Gulzar serving as a script consultant for early issues. Even M G Ramachandran featured as a character in Tamil comics. “Comics have been strong allies of journalism; they allow you to sneak in even where cinema can’t,” observes Amruta.
The rise of the graphic novel
By the late 1990s, Indian graphic storytelling had begun to move far beyond superheroes and adventure tales. The medium evolved into a powerful tool for social commentary, tackling themes that mainstream publishing often shied away from — love and relationships, body image, feminism, sexuality, postpartum depression, domestic abuse, and the aspirations of women, including those from rural India. Among the most influential voices was Manjula Padmanabhan, whose work challenged conventional representations of women. Through characters such as the unconventional Sukhi — an oversized, unapologetically lazy woman — Padmanabhan explored themes such as motherhood, postpartum blues, and emotional abuse.
A significant turning point came with publisher V K Karthika, who helped bring the graphic novel into India’s mainstream publishing landscape. “Under her editorial vision, graphic narratives were no longer relegated to a niche readership and the stories became more diverse and inclusive, featuring queer voices, androgynous protagonists, and narratives that reflected contemporary Indian society,” says Amruta, whose own work
 Kari
 features in the exhibition. It follows a queer woman navigating with love, loss and loneliness in Mumbai. Another landmark was Orijit Sen’s 
River of Stories
, widely regarded as India’s first graphic novel. It demonstrated the medium’s potential for activism, weaving together environmental concerns, the struggles against large dams, mining, long before climate change became part of everyday discussion.
Can AI tell stories?
The exhibition concludes with a pressing question at the centre of creative conversations today: What happens when artificial intelligence enters the artistic process? “The answer is measured rather than alarmist. While technology will undoubtedly transform how stories are produced, creativity, lived experience, empathy and critical thinking will remain uniquely human qualities that no tool can fully replace,” shares Amruta.
STANDOUT WORKS:
- Visual traditions of Gond and Madhubani art
- Rajkumari’s indigenous literature in Chota Nagpuri
- G. R. Santosh’s work on tribal exploitation and artistic independence
- Suits, a graphic novel where Mumbai sewage workers wear suits

stories.headline: Karnataka schools association seeks uniform national formula for RTE reimbursement
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: While Tamil Nadu pays private schools Rs 25,155 to Rs 33,806 as Right to Education (RTE) reimbursement per child, Madhya Pradesh has calculated the per-child expenditure at Rs 4,419.
The observation was made by the Associated Managements of Primary and Secondary Schools of 
Karnataka
 (KAMS), which has been seeking a uniform national methodology for deciding per-child expenditure.
The association has compiled per-child expenditure figures for states across the country. Karnataka pays Rs 8,000 to Rs 16,000. Among the high payers are Delhi (Rs 19,176), Tripura (Rs 21,138), and Maharashtra (Rs 17,670).
Andhra Pradesh has different reimbursement rates based on geography: it is Rs 8,000 for urban areas, Rs 6,500 for rural areas, and Rs 5,100 for tribal areas. “Several states continue to reimburse schools based on notifications issued between 2013 and 2018, despite significant increases in elementary education budgets, enhanced central assistance under Samagra Shiksha, and substantial investments in digital education, infrastructure, teacher-capacity building and other educational initiatives.
 The absence of periodic revision has created wide disparities in reimbursement across states under the same central legislation,” observed D Shashi Kumar, secretary, KAMS, in his letter to the Centre.
“In the interest of transparency, cooperative federalism, and faithful implementation of the RTE Act, we humbly request the govt of India to prescribe a uniform national methodology for determining per-child expenditure and to direct every state and union territory implementing the Act to publish an annual audited per-child expenditure declaration in the public domain,” he added.
As per the Union ministry, the number of seats earmarked under RTE quota in Karnataka was nearly 1.7 lakh in 2025-26.

stories.headline: MP Surya urges Karnataka govt for stronger Rera enforcement
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Bangalore South MP 
Tejasvi Surya
 has urged 
Karnataka
 govt to strengthen the proposed Karnataka Apartment (Ownership and Management) Bill, 2026, by ensuring it complements Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA), 2016, rather than creating a parallel legal framework.
In a representation to chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 on July 31, Surya welcomed the govt’s move to replace the decades-old Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act, 1972, and Karnataka Ownership Flats Act, 1972, with unified legislation. However, he said the primary issue faced by apartment owners was not the absence of laws but the lack of effective enforcement of existing rights, particularly regarding transfer of common areas and transparent apartment governance.
Surya, who suggested seven points, highlighted that Section 17 of RERA, dealing with transfer of title of common areas to apartment associations, should be operationalised through the proposed legislation. He recommended that the bill must mandate time-bound transfer of common areas and underlying land to registered apartment associations.
The legislation should ultimately strengthen RERA implementation and provide a transparent, accountable framework for lakhs of apartment owners across Karnataka, the BJP MP said.

stories.headline: Aug 30 deadline looms, Gruha Jyothi drive hits locked houses
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: It’s a familiar story, but a different exercise: huge apartment complexes with locked houses, and residents staying overseas. This is the crux of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The story is annoyingly similar in the audit of Gruha Jyothi verification drive, slowing the state’s effort to weed out ineligible beneficiaries under the flagship free electricity scheme.
With the Aug 30 deadline looming, the verification drive has audited nearly 55% of the state’s 1.6 crore-plus beneficiaries ever since its launch on July 1, though locked houses have emerged as one of the biggest roadblocks.
The drive started after the state govt decided to remove ineligible beneficiaries, including those allegedly registered as voters in other states while availing benefits in 
Karnataka
. The exercise involves linking beneficiaries’ voter ID details with their electricity connections to ensure that only eligible households continue to receive free power.
Since meter readers and Escom officials have been deployed for the exercise, regular monthly meter readings were suspended. Consumers were issued average electricity bills based on their consumption over the previous three months.
Reviewing the progress of the drive on a daily basis, senior Bescom officials said although electricity meters are installed at centralised locations in flats, every beneficiary must be physically present to fill out the declaration form, have their photograph taken and upload the details through the mobile application.
“Most apartment residents are away at work during the day, while some simply do not turn up despite repeated visits. This makes it difficult to complete the verification in a single visit,” a meter reader in Bengaluru said. “Our meter readers have been leaving messages with neighbours about absentee citizens, but to no avail,” a senior Bescom engineer said.
Several consumers narrated a different experience. “No meter reader visited our house this month. We received an average electricity bill through the app. When we contacted Bescom, we were asked to visit a kiosk for verification. But Bescom’s communication had clearly stated that officials would visit every beneficiary’s doorstep,” said a beneficiary from Jambu Savari Dinne in JP Nagar. A resident from Soladevanahalli echoed a similar concern. “Officials were sitting at a nearby teashop and residents had to go there with documents,” the consumer alleged.
Bescom managing director N Shivashankara said there would be no tolerance for staff failing to conduct doorstep verification. “Consumers can lodge a complaint through Bescom helpline, and we will take action,” he said.
About locked houses, Shivashankara said officials make at least two visits. “We’re examining how to handle such cases: should they be asked to visit the division office or should we have a new mechanism. We’ll discuss this with the energy minister and the govt before a decision is made,” he said.
Inset Box: Performance Of Escoms In Gruhajyothi Verification  ( Table has been shared via E-mail)

stories.headline: Brent falls to $80, goverment vows to mitigate volatility
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Global benchmark Brent crude fell to a three-week low on Tuesday, amid renewed optimism over reopening of Strait of Hormuz, after senior US officials indicated that a deal with Iran could be possible.
Brent was trading below the $80-a-barrel mark (9.15 pm) on Tuesday, its lowest level since July 13, down almost 5% in a day on expectations of easing supply disruptions. Latest data available on PPAC website pegged the price of Indian basket at $88.12 a barrel. Global oil prices have remained volatile, amid renewed US-Iran conflict and disruption to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which handles nearly a fifth of the world's energy trade, as well as Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Govt, however, said it will continue to adopt appropriate fiscal and administrative measures to mitigate the impact of future fuel price volatility, while maintaining fiscal sustainability. Responding to a question in Rajya Sabha, minister of state for finance Pankaj Chaudhary said despite severe disruptions in global energy markets during West Asia conflict, measures taken by govt helped cushion the impact on consumers and the domestic economy.
"Brent crude prices peaked at $138.2 per barrel in April 2026, exerting upward pressure on global energy prices and domestic producer prices. However, to protect consumers, govt limited the increase in domestic retail prices of petrol and diesel to a marginal level," Chaudhary said.
He added that the impact on consumer prices remained relatively contained, with average CPI inflation at 3.9% in April-June 2026, below RBI's inflation target of 4% (+/-2%).
The minister also said that reduction in central excise duty on petrol and diesel by Rs 10 per litre in March 2026 protected consumers from elevated international crude prices. It also partly offset the under-recoveries absorbed by state-run oil marketing companies, enabling them to continue supplying fuel without disruption.

stories.headline: Tax bill aims to woo global investors
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: FM 
Nirmala Sitharaman
 on Tuesday moved the Taxational and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, proposing fresh steps to woo overseas investors and fund managers into the country, while offering predictability to electronics goods makers and component suppliers.
The bill will also seek Parliamentary approval for the tax changes introduced through an amendment to attract foreign investors in govt securities.
Seeking to simplify rules to attract fund managers to India, govt has sought to cut down the list of conditions that discouraged them from being based in the country as they feared that the entire foreign fund may be taxable here. Now, the idea is to retain only those provisions that are essential to prevent misuse and round tripping of money by Indian residents, officials said.
"A fund manager can now relocate to India without the foreign fund being treated as doing business in India. The expectation is that many managers of global funds will move to India, bringing high value activity and jobs with them. This proposal will also apply to International Financial Services Centre (Gift City) to provide flexibility of location to the fund managers," an official said.
Besides, the Centre has sought to provide simpler rules for data centres, which were offered tax concessions - but with layers of approvals and govt notifications. 
The bill removes the approval requirements and allows Indian data centres to be run on a leased basis - instead of being under direct ownership.
In case of electronics, govt has made the income of a foreign company tax free when it supplies machinery and tooling to an Indian electronics manufacturer for a period of 15 years, instead of five years at present. Electronics goods have been clearly defined and include mobile phones, laptops and computers, tablets, servers and their key parts and accessories.
Besides, electronics component suppliers, which store components in bonded warehouses for local manufacturers, have been given incentives to ensure just in time delivery of inputs that are critical.
To boost diamond trade, govt has also proposed to fully exempt the income of overseas diamond miners and traders connected to them from selling precious stones in special economic zones for 15 years. The definition of diamond has also been widened.

stories.headline: United Spirits contests FSSAI's flavouring order, petitions HC
stories.deck: United Spirits finds itself at the center of a legal battle, opposing a food regulator’s decree about its McDowell's No. 1 Rum labeling. The FSSAI asserts that flavors typical of rum and whisky are not permissible in spirits. Inspections have uncovered that various manufacturers employed neutral alcohols augmented with flavoring agents, resulting in these products being deemed subpar according to…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Diageo-owned United Spirits has moved Bombay high court against a Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (
FSSAI
) order concerning McDowell's No. 1 Rum manufactured at its Baramati plant.
The company disclosed the legal challenge on Tuesday, days after the food regulator barred the sale of certain rum and whisky products made by United Spirits and other liquor companies. FSSAI said manufacturers cannot add "rum flavour" to rum or "whisky flavour" to whisky and market them as regular spirits.
United Spirits challenged the regulator's June 29 order on Aug 1. The company said the order pertains to the labelling of a single product manufactured at its Baramati facility, which FSSAI alleged was not compliant with food safety regulations.
"Based on legal advice, the company is of the view that the declarations on the product labels in question are in compliance with the current applicable legal and regulatory framework in India and are consistent with long-standing industry practice," United Spirits said in a regulatory filing. The company added that the order has had no material financial or operational impact so far. It declined to comment further as the matter is sub judice.
According to FSSAI, the characteristic taste and aroma of rum and whisky should be derived from their ingredients and the manufacturing process, including fermentation, distillation and ageing. However, inspections found that some manufacturers were using neutral alcohol with little inherent flavour and adding flavouring agents to replicate the taste and aroma of rum or whisky.
The regulator said such products should instead be labelled as "rum-flavoured spirit" or "whisky-flavoured spirit" and classified the products tested as "substandard" under the Food Safety and Standards Act.

stories.headline: MDR to help fintechs recover costs, boost their IPO hopes
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: India's payment industry has long been calling for higher subsidies or a controlled introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) to recover transaction costs. The decision to allow MDR or higher value business payments will help to turn many business models sustainable and thereby increase competition in an industry that is currently a near duopoly of PhonePe and Google Pay.
The introduction of a MDR will boost the prospect of companies awaiting IPOs such as PhonePe, Razorpay, PayU, PayNearby, and Innoviti. Fintechs are backing the move. Industry executives said that it will open up avenues for companies to get compensated for the operational and customer acquisition costs they have to bear for processing large volumes of transactions every day. Besides, if firms are able to make some money through UPI transactions, they can also innovate and bolster their systems at an individual level to check frauds, they said. "The ecosystem (fintech and banks) spends anywhere around Rs 10,000-12,000 crore every year to power UPI transactions. Of this, the govt gives only about Rs 2000 crore (by way of incentives). The rest gets lost," said an executive with a fintech firm on condition of anonymity.
PhonePe, Razorpay, PayU Among Cos Eyeing Public Issue
At present, UPI transactions are free for merchants. Walmart's PhonePe and Google Pay hold the bulk of the market share.
UPI processes nearly 23 billion payment transactions every month. 
For now, it is understood that the govt will introduce MDR only on large value transactions. In a note, Jefferies said that a 15-30 bps MDR on M (peer-to-merchant) transactions above Rs 2,000 can potentially generate Rs 5,000-10,000 crore in revenues for payment platforms. While such transactions made up only 4% of volumes in FY26, they accounted for 67% in value terms. "As the larger part of the incremental cost is incurred by merchant acquirers, they may retain a larger share," analysts at Jefferies said.
The fintech ecosystem has for long been calling for monetisation of UPI payments to enable sustainable growth of the industry. Also, there is a thinking that absence of MDR is leading to an oligopolistic situation with Google and Walmart dominating the market. But MDR on UPI is complex because govt has repeatedly assured that UPI will be free.
Amrish Rau, CEO at Pine Labs said that the costs to fund expansion of UPI through continued investments in tech, IT, innovation and cyber-security have increased by almost 300% over the last 12-24 months. "While there should be some recovery of these investments, P transactions and charges to consumers-should continue to remain zero," Rau said.

stories.headline: Govt ups LIC offer size, OFS India's biggest
stories.deck: The government has announced an extra four percent sale in LIC’s offering, responding to considerable interest revealed by a 3.3 times subscription on day one. This strong demand from institutional buyers led to the exercise of the green shoe option, anticipating a total raise of roughly Rs 31,400 crore from this share sale. Retail investors can participate by bidding on the last day.
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Govt on Tuesday opted to sell an additional 4% in LIC in the ongoing offer for sale (OFS) for the life insurance major as the issue was subscribed 3.3 times on the opening day. Including the green shoe option that takes the total offer size to 82.2 crore shares, govt is expected to mop up about Rs 31,400 crore from the offer at the base price of Rs 382 per share, making it the largest ever OFS in the Indian market. Indications are that the total fund mobilisation could get a further boost on the closing day.
Data on NSE showed the indicative price for the offer at Rs 383.84 per share. If all the 82.2 crore shares are sold at that price, the total offer size would be close to 31,600 crore. Officials said that over Rs 28,000 crore has already been mopped up taking the disinvestment receipts for the current fiscal year to Rs 50,000 crore, against the target of Rs 80,000 crore for the full year, excluding asset monetisation, which has generated a little over Rs 6,000 crore so far.
"This enthusiastic participation reflects robust investor confidence and the depth of India's capital markets. In view of the exceptional demand, govt has decided to exercise the green shoe option. 
Retail investors get to bid tomorrow (on Wednesday). Make the most of this opportunity," DIPAM secretary Arunish Chawla said in a social media post.
On Tuesday, backed by strong institutional demand for LIC shares, govt said it will sell an additional 50.6 crore LIC shares, to take the total offer size to 82.2 crore shares. The base offer was for 31.6 crore shares, translating to 2.5% of the life insurance major's equity capital.
At the close of Tuesday's bidding in the OFS, data from NSE showed that the total demand was for nearly 94.5 crore shares. Only non-retail investors were allowed to bid on the first day of the offer. On Wednesday, the closing day of the offer, retail investors will also be allowed to participate.
In the OFS, 8.2 crore shares, or 10% of the offer is reserved for retail investors and another 50 lakh shares are reserved for LIC's employees. Since a successful closure of the offer will bring in another 82.2 crore LIC shares in the market, on Tuesday on BSE the stock closed nearly 8% lower at Rs 391, compared to the offer price of Rs 382.

stories.headline: Sachin Siwach, Preeti Pawar eye Asian Games gold after record-breaking Boxing medal haul at CWG 2026
stories.deck: Speaking to ANI, Sachin, who secured a gold medal in the men's 60 kg final, said that seeing the national flag hoisted after the gold medal win is a "different kind of happiness" and a reason why they all play sport
stories.bodyText:
Indian pugilists Sachin Siwach and Preeti Pawar have their eyes set on Asian Games gold following their gold medal wins at the recently concluded Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow.
The Indian boxing contingent, which pulled off the country's best CWG 2026 medal haul with seven gold medals and overall 10 medals, received a warm welcome at the Delhi Airport.
Speaking to ANI, Sachin, who secured a gold medal in the men's 60 kg final, said that seeing the national flag hoisted after the gold medal win is a "different kind of happiness" and a reason why they all play sport.
"When the national flag is hoisted, there is a different kind of happiness. This is what we play for. I want to bring gold from the Asian Games. I want to tell everyone to keep believing like this and keep encouraging us," said Siwach.
Sachin staged a remarkable comeback to defeat Namibia's Tryagain Morning Ndevelo by a 3-2 split decision in a thrilling men's 60 kg final.
Also, Preeti has her eyes set on not only the Asian Games this year in Japan taking place from September 19 onwards, but also the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, saying, "Thank you very much to everyone who came here to receive us. Our next target is the Asian Games and the LA 2028 Olympics. We cannot express our happiness on hearing the National Anthem play there. It is something that you can only feel."
The 2022 Asian Games bronze medalist Preeti secured the women's 54kg gold medal at the CWG 2026 after defeating Canada's Scarlett Delgado by unanimous decision in the final on Saturday.
The 2026 Games were hosted under a compact format, leading to the removal of major Indian medal-earning events like shooting, hockey, wrestling, and badminton.
India finished fourth in the medals table at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.
India officially began its journey towards hosting the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Amdavad as the Commonwealth Games Flag was ceremonially handed over during a spectacular Closing Ceremony that celebrated the conclusion of Glasgow 2026 and looked ahead to the historic centenary edition of the Games.
Published - August 05, 2026 01:30 am IST

stories.headline: Fulham sign Gonzalo, Palacios from Real Madrid
stories.deck: Arbeloa coached Real's youth and ‌reserve teams before taking over ‌the ⁠senior side in January to ⁠replace compatriot Xabi Alonso. He left Real at the end of the season and joined ​Fulham in July
stories.bodyText:
Fulham have signed forward Gonzalo Garcia and midfielder Cesar Palacios from Real Madrid on five-year contracts, the Premier League club said on Monday (August 3, 2026).
Palacios, 21, and Real academy product Garcia, 22, will reunite with former coach Alvaro Arbeloa at Fulham.
Arbeloa coached Real's youth and reserve teams before taking over the senior side in January to replace compatriot Xabi Alonso. He left Real at the end of the season and joined Fulham in July.
Garcia scored 13 goals in 51 appearances for Real in all competitions and won the Champions League and LaLiga in 2024. The transfer fee was not disclosed but British media reported Fulham had paid around £34 million ($45 million) for the forward.
Palacios has also signed a deal running until June 2031, with Fulham holding an option to extend it by a further year.
The midfielder made seven senior appearances for Real, making his debut in the Copa del Rey against Albacete and also featured in the Champions League.
The transfer fee was not disclosed, but media reports put the deal at around £8.5 million.
Fulham begin their Premier League campaign by hosting Chelsea on August 24.
Published - August 05, 2026 01:23 am IST

stories.headline: FIFA executive Arsene Wenger backs decision to drop Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan
stories.deck: Wenger's statement on the controversy came after a letter from UEFA's lawyers to Infantino threatening legal action named the French coaching great among 18 executives whose data and communications should be retained as potential evidence
stories.bodyText:
FIFA executive Arsène Wenger on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) distanced himself from Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in future World Cup profits to private investors and said it was “absolutely necessary” to drop the proposal.
Wenger's statement on the controversy came after a letter from UEFA's lawyers to Infantino threatening legal action named the French coaching great among 18 executives whose data and communications should be retained as potential evidence.
“I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports,” said Wenger, who was hired by Infantino in 2019 and is FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development.
The statement by the former Arsenal coach did not name Infantino.
“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity,” Wenger wrote.
Infantino withdrew his $20 billion proposal early on Saturday (August 1) after a furious backlash by global soccer officials, including European body UEFA warning of a boycott of all FIFA games and events.
Published - August 05, 2026 01:19 am IST

stories.bodyText:
Algeria parted ways with coach Vladimir Petkovic on Monday (August 3, 2026), despite the Bosnian signing a contract extension before the World Cup where the team reached the last 32.
The 62-year-old took the helm in February 2024 and renewed his contract until 2028 before the World Cup got underway.
"The Algerian Football Federation announce that their contractual relationship with the national team head coach, Mr. Vladimir Petkovic, and his coaching staff has officially come to an end today, on a mutual agreement between the two parties," the local soccer governing body said in a statement.
Algeria made it to the round of 32 at the 48-team World Cup in North America as one of the best eight third-placed teams, losing 2-0 to Switzerland.
They begin qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations in September, where they have been drawn in Group I alongside Zambia, Togo and Burundi.

stories.headline: ​Top spot: On the new phase of the Khelo India Scheme
stories.deck: India needs to upgrade infrastructure, train coaches
stories.bodyText:
One of the biggest impediments to India’s aspiration to bid for the 2036 Olympics is the lack of enough world-class performers. For India, a prospective host, targeting a prestigious top-10 finish is a humongous task. In the 21st century, the country achieved its best-ever result of 48th with seven medals at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and was 71st with six medals at Paris 2024. India needs to win approximately 30 to 40 medals, including gold in double digits, to be in the elite club. To chase this Olympic dream, the Union Cabinet has approved an allocation of ₹29,054 crore — an eight-fold increase — for the new phase of the Khelo India Scheme. The primary goal of this ambitious grassroots programme is to tap talent early for the 2036 Olympics. It aims to increase Khelo India centres, State and National centres of excellence and accredited academies from roughly one per district — more than 1,000 centres at present — to an average of two or three. Involving schools and clubs, encouraging talented children to compete in club-level events, upgrading facilities, and assimilating grassroot-coaches and technical officials are essential ingredients of the wholesome scheme.
A novel concept of upgrading the knowledge of local coaches by helping them overcome the language barrier posed by English, the formation of a National Coach Accreditation Board to standardise coaching and better utilisation of physical education teachers are expected to impart correct training at the basic level. In sync with the National Education Policy, the Khelo India Feeder Schools and Khelo India Utkrishta Vidyalaya initiatives are designed to integrate education and sports. The existing Khelo India Athletes programme, with 2,904 athletes, and the new Emerging Khelo India Athletes initiative aim to expand the talent pool to around 28,000. Talent identification, digitisation of the sports ecosystem to maintain data on every athlete, and a bottom-to-top communication channel are its key components. The overall outlay, including assistance to National Sports Federations, stands at a staggering ₹36,441 crore for 2026-31. However, the biggest challenge will be effective and transparent implementation of the scheme. Enabling talent to graduate to the highest level, already backed by the Target Olympic Podium Scheme, with an eye on the 2036 Olympics and beyond will be crucial. The 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad will be an immediate test. The other major hurdle for India’s attempt to emerge as a sporting power is its dubious distinction as a doping hub. Strict anti-doping measures, promotion of a sports culture by maximising the scope of the Fit India Movement, and a focus on grassroots development must go hand-in-hand to achieve the desired results.
Published - August 05, 2026 12:10 am IST
